correctness.rationale: For the specified positive parameters 0<h<a, R>w and S>b, only the rectangle top edge intersects the triangle boundary near t=0. Direct integration of horizontal section width 2w(a-y)/(a+b) yields f(t)=w/(a+b)(he^t+b)(2a+b-he^t). Writing x=he^t, the logarithmic-curvature numerator factors exactly as −2xG(x) times a positive scale, G(x)=a x²+(4ab+2b²)x−ab(2a+b). Independently simplified the symbolic factorization and substitution of h*=a sqrt(b(2a+b))/(a+b+sqrt(b(2a+b))): both residuals vanish. G is strictly increasing for x>0, G(0)<0; log-concavity on a two-sided neighborhood holds iff h>h*. At h=h*, negative t produces positive curvature, so equality is not an exception. Bar-On coordinates yield h*=4/3 and curvature 26/441. This is an exact local proof, not a finite grid assertion.

value.rationale: The source example is a canonical one-axis counterexample to relaxation of symmetry in a planar B-property. Varying the natural triangle dimensions and the sole active rectangle cut gives a complete, exact phase boundary, including a nontrivial equality-point distinction. This converts a one-off example into a motivated local classification. It does not purport to cover other active-side regimes; its elementary algebra does not by itself make the specific phase classification routine or known.

limitations: Classification is local in t near 0 with exactly one rectangle side active; no broader B-theorem or novel parameter-free assertion.
